[Since Po vide order dated 05.01.2016] Cc No. 38997/2016 Page No. 2/10 Da vs Ramesh Chand & Ors Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisi
texts.facts: . 2. As per the complaint, on 22.06.2001, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) FI Shri S.P. Singh and FI Shri S.B. Sharma under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri S.K. Nanda visited the premises of M/s Ramesh Trading Co., Shop No. 1345 Qutab Road, Sadar Bazar, Delhi 110006, where accused No. 1 Ramesh Chand was found conducting the business of food articles for sale for human consumption, including "Electrolyte Sports Drink" (ready for sale). The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase Da vs Ramesh Chand & Ors on 17 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137625258/ 2 a sample of "Electrolyte Sports Drink" from the vendor for analysis. The sample consisted of 3x600 ml. Electrolyte Sports Drink in sealed plastic bottle taken as such in original condition bearing identical label declaration . The sample was taken under the supervision of Local Health Authority, Sh. SK Nanda. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts. Each sample part containing one originally sealed bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the Counter part. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Ramesh Chander and the price of the sample was also given to him vide vendor's receipt dated 22-06-2001. DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by Food Inspector were signed by accused No. 1 Ramesh Chander and the other witness Sh.S.B. Shanna, F.I. Before starting sample proceedings efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward. then Sh. S.B. Sharma was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. SKN/LHA/0368 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be misbranded The report of the Public Analyst is as follows :- "The sample is misbranded as there is violation of Rule 24, Rule 32 f and i ." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused no. 1 Ramesh Chander was the vendor cum partner of M/s Ramesh Trading Co, Shop No. 1345 Qutab Road, Sadar Bazar, Delhi-110006 at the time of sampling. M/s Ramesh Trading Co. is a partnership firm as per Partnership Deed dated 25-12-2000. There are two partners of the firm vendor Ramesh Chander and accused No. 3 Robin Arora so both partners along with firm are liable as there is no nominee appointed under PFA Act by the firm. Accused No. 2 M/s Ramesh Trading Co. has purchased the sample commodity from M/s Horizon Agencies B-120, Shivaji Vihar, New Delhi- 110027 vide Bill No. 101837 dated 14-06-01. M/s Horizon Agencies is a partnership concern. As per partnership deed dt. DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors 8.04.82 there are two partners i.e. Sh. Deep Chopra and Smt. Baljinder Kaur. As there is no nominee appointed so both the partners along with firm are in-charge and responsible for the above firm. M/s Horizon agencies have purchased the sample commodity from M/s L-Comps & Impex Private Ltd. 182/63, Industrial Area Phase-I, Chandigarh --160002(India). It is an Importer Firm of the sample commodity M/s L-Comps & Impex Private Ltd. is a Company having two Directors i.e. Sh. Punkaj Gupta and Sh. Puneet Gupta. The Company has nominated Sh. Anu Sharma, Manager (Purchase & Liaison) as nominee of the Company under PFA Act so Company and its Nominee are the delinquent parties 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the Court on 04.12.2002 alleging violation of Rule 24, 32 f & i and section 5 of of PFA Rules, which is punishable under Section 16(1)(a) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 by the accused. Da vs Ramesh Chand & Ors on 17 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137625258/ 3 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 04.12.2002. Based on the report of the PA notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Rule 24, Rule 32 (f) & (i) of PFA Rules to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. During the trial, accused No. 1 (also representing accused No. 2) has expired and DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors proceedings against him were abated. The accused No. 8 has was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 05.01.2016. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh S.K. Nanda and PW-3 FI Shri N.N. Sharma. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh and FI Shri S.B. Sharma were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA S.K. Nanda. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of three sealed bottle of Electrolyte Sport Drink of 600 Ml each, bearing identical label declaration, dividing the sample into three counterparts, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in form VI Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. The vendor also disclosed the source of purchase of sample commodity vide bill No. 1018857, accordingly notice under section 14 A Ex.PW1/D addressing to M/s Horizon Agencies B 120 Shiviji Vihar, New Delhi was also prepared at the spot and sent through registered post on the next working day. Thereafter, one counter part of the sample commodity was deposited in intact condition with the PA on 25.6.01 i.e next working day vide receipt Ex.PW1/E and another copy of Memo From VII in a separately sealed envelop. The remaining two counter parts of sample in intact condition along with two copies of report in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 25.6.01 DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors i.e next working day vide receipt Ex.PW1/F with the intimation that one counter part of the sample in intact condition has already been deposited with the PA. Thereafter PA report Ex.PW1/G was received according to which sample was found misbranded for violation of Rule, 24, 32 (f) & (i), as mentioned therein at portion X. During investigation , PW-1 FI S.P.Singh sent a letter to vendor and received photocopy of Registration Certificate and Partnership-Deed mark 'X & Y' alongwith photocopy of Bill of purchase mark 'Z'. As there was some confusion in respect of partners of vendor's firm, PW-1 FI S.P. Singh sent a letter Ex. PW1/H to Vendor and received reply Ex. PW1/H-l informing that Smt. Krishna Wanti had expired. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh also sent a letter Ex. PW1/l to STO Ward No. 31 to disclose the constitution of M/s Ramesh Trading Company and as per reply the firm was partnership firm having two partners i.e. Ramesh Chand Arora and Krishna Wanti. After the death of Smt. Krishna Wanti, Sh. Rohan Arora was inducted a partnership-deed mark 'Y'. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh sent a letter Ex. PW1/J to M/s Horizon Agencies and received reply Ex. PW1/J1 wherein they informed that they purchased the sample commodity from M/s L.Comps & lmpex Pvt Ltd, who was the importer of the sample commodity and name of the Director was informed as Puneet Gupta and supplied the photocopy of Bill of purchase mark 'Z1'. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh also sent a letter Ex. PW1/K to STO Ward No. 57 to disclose the constitution of M/s Horizon Agencies and as per reply, Sh. Deep Chopra and Mrs. Baljinder Kaur were the partners of the said firm. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh sent five letters Ex. PW1/L1 to L5 to M/s L.Comps & lmpex Pvt. Ltd and received three replies Ex.PW1/L6 DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors to L8 informing that the name of the Directors and nomination in favour of Sh. Anu Sharma , Da vs Ramesh Chand & Ors on 17 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137625258/ 4 copy of Nomination in form Vll Ex.PW1/L9. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh also sent two letters Ex.PW1/M1 & M-2 to Registrar Company to disclose the constitution of M/s L.Comps & lmpex Pvt. Ltd but no reply was received. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh also sent a letter Ex. PW1/N to CMO Chandigarh to confirm the nomination in favour of Sh. Anu Sharma and received reply Ex. PW1/N1 that they accepted their nomination for one person and provided the photocopy of form Vlll in favour of Sh. Anu Sharma. After completion of the investigation, the complete case file along with all the statutory documents were sent to the then Director Sh. K.S. Wahi through LHA, who after going through the entire case file, applied his mind and gave the sanction for prosecution Ex.PW1/O against the accused person. Thereafter the present complaint Ex.PW3/A was filed by PW3 Shri N.N. Sharma in the Court and then the intimation letter was sent along with the PA report by registered post to accused. The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 03.12.2016 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In their defence evidence, the accused No. 1 Ramesh Chander examined himself as DW-1 and placed on record the source of purchase of sample commodity vide Ex.DW1/A to D. Accused also examined Deep Chopra partner of M/s Horizon Agency as DW-2 DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors and placed on record the bill ExDW2/A through which the juices were purchased. Thereafter, the defence evidence was closed vide order dated 07.03.2017 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: Regarding misbranding the defence has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in S.S. Gokul Krishanan & Others vs State 2009(1) FAC 132 to argue that there was a policy of the complainant department of 1985 numbered as Policy No F6(228)/85/ENF/PFA wherein a decision was taken to give a written warning to the offenders with regard to any deficiency in respect of Rule 32 of the PFA Act. The judgment of Gokul Krishnan (supra) has also been followed in the judgment of M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State & Another Crl.MC 439/2008 dated 20.01.2011 DA vs Ramesh Chand & Ors and recently in Hello Minerals Water PVT LTD & Ors vs State CRL.MC.224/2016 dated 10.01.2018. 12.
